basis: Mandibular and facial skeletal dysostosis defines the syndrome; evidence for common damage to additional organs is insufficient.
Neonatal autoimmune scleroderma affects skin; common internal-organ damage is not established for this neonatal entity.
Malignant bone-forming tumor, usually arising in bone; pulmonary metastases are a minority complication.
Generalized lymphatic vascular dysplasia with intestinal lymphangiectasia in 7/7; pulmonary lymphangiectasia in 6/7 and pleural involvement in 4/7.
Peripheral neuroepithelial malignancy classified as a nervous-system neoplasm; no additional consistently affected organ is established.
PURA-related encephalopathy with developmental impairment and brain abnormalities; ptosis affects eyelid function in 30-79%. Respiratory distress alone does not establish lung damage.
Defined by transient monocular visual loss from retinal ischemia; underlying carotid disease is a separate condition.
Hereditary motor neuron degeneration; weakness and muscle wasting reflect denervation rather than a primary muscle disease.
Degeneration and necrosis of the basal ganglia cause developmental regression and progressive movement impairment.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder defined by encephalopathy and myopathy; marrow and urinary abnormalities lack evidence of involvement in at least 30%.
Mature T-cell lymphoma is a hematologic malignancy and meets the lymphoma mechanism axis; extranodal organ involvement varies.
Chronic rubbing and scratching produce localized skin thickening; the definition does not establish an autoimmune or immune-mediated disease.
Biallelic RPE65 disease causes retinal degeneration and visual loss.
Congenital distal joint contractures and hand/foot deformities define the disorder; hearing impairment occurs in only 1-4%.
Cutis laxa in 8/8; craniosynostosis 6/8 and joint abnormalities; learning disability 3/7; hearing impairment 3/8. Proptosis alone does not establish visual damage.
Astrocytic tumor arising in the central nervous system; additional organ damage is not inherent to the diagnosis.
Hereditary susceptibility defined by neuroblastoma of sympathetic neural tissue; the label identifies the defining tumor lineage, without implying an existing tumor.
Degenerative disease of the peripheral retina.
Localized nonsuppurative inflammation and swelling of costal cartilage; chest pain does not indicate cardiac disease.
Linear skin defects in 11/11 and microphthalmia in 10/11 define the syndrome; developmental impairment in 2/9 is below the involvement threshold.
Mucinous cystic neoplasm arising from intrahepatic bile ducts.
Squamous cell carcinoma originates in the pharynx, which belongs to the pulmonary axis under the specified mapping.
Developmental disability, dermal melanocytosis and strabismus define the syndrome; strabismus occurs in 3/3. Chronic kidney disease and reduced GFR are frequent (30-79%).
The diagnosed disease is myocardial injury and dysfunction caused by doxorubicin; cardiac damage defines this concept.
Inherited hepatic bile-acid transport disorder defined by hypercholanemia and fat malabsorption; pruritus alone does not establish skin damage.
